about: The open Snapmaker/U1 ecosystem as data. Studio matches a project's real traits against these entries to suggest which tool is the right next step. Adding a tool is a pull request against this file — no code change. See docs/EXTENDING.md for the schema and the rules for what qualifies.
confidence_note: Studio only claims a tool is installed when it found the executable on disk. Everything else is presented as a link, never as a detected install.

tools.name: Snapmaker Orca
tools.role: Slices your project for the U1. This is the default next step.
tools.install_hint: Download the installer from the Snapmaker Orca releases page.

recommend_when.reason: This project already targets the Snapmaker U1, so the official slicer opens it with the right profile.
An STL has no print settings yet — Snapmaker Orca is where you choose them.
This project was authored for another printer. Prepare a U1 copy in Studio first — then Snapmaker Orca opens that copy with U1 settings.

tools.name: FOrcaSlicer
tools.role: A community Snapmaker Orca fork that lets each of the U1's four heads run a different nozzle size, and can wrap one material as a shell over another.
tools.install_hint: Download a build from the FOrcaSlicer releases page. It is a separate application; it does not replace Snapmaker Orca.
tools.caution: A research-preview community fork, independent of Snapmaker. Review its output before a long print.

recommend_when.reason: This project already uses more than one nozzle size, which is exactly what this fork is built for.
Painted multi-colour regions are where its shell-over-core mode changes the result.

tools.name: OrcaSlicer ImageMap
tools.role: An OrcaSlicer fork that prints a raster image into a surface, and converts between textures, vertex colours and painted 3MF regions.
tools.install_hint: Download a build from its releases page. It is a separate application.
tools.caution: A community fork, independent of Snapmaker, and self-described as beta.

recommend_when.reason: This model carries image-texture data, which most slicers throw away and this fork can actually print.

tools.name: MakerWorld to Snapmaker U1
tools.role: A browser extension that converts a MakerWorld project to a U1 project at the moment you download it, keeping the creator's own print profile.
tools.install_hint: Install it in your browser, then download the project again from MakerWorld.

recommend_when.reason: This looks like a MakerWorld download authored for another printer. Converting it in the browser next time keeps the creator's profile intact from the start.

tools.notes: Its own notices state that some conversion logic and reference data derive from a PolyForm-Noncommercial project. Studio implements the same compatibility behaviours independently and uses no code or data from it.

tools.name: U1 Print Hub
tools.role: A local web dashboard for one or more U1s: send files, map toolheads, track spools, watch a print.
tools.install_hint: Download a single-file binary from its releases page and open it in your browser.

recommend_when.reason: This project is already sliced, so the next step is getting it onto a printer rather than back into a slicer.

tools.name: Snapmaker U1 Toolkit
tools.role: A toolkit that slices and uploads prints from a terminal or from your phone over Telegram, and starts a print only after a human approves it against a fresh photo of the bed.
tools.install_hint: Clone the repository and follow its README. Needs a Linux or WSL host; there is no desktop GUI, though it can be driven from a phone over Telegram.

recommend_when.reason: This project is already sliced, so this toolkit can send it to the printer without opening a slicer again.

tools.caution: Young, and it expects a Linux or WSL host rather than native Windows or macOS. Its safety gate asks a human to approve every print start — read its README first.

tools.name: Fluidd (on your printer)
tools.role: The web interface the U1 already serves. Nothing to install — it runs on the printer.
tools.install_hint: Turn on Advanced Mode on the printer's touchscreen, then open the printer's IP address in your browser.

recommend_when.reason: Once a project is sliced, the printer's own web interface is the simplest place to send it — nothing to install.

tools.name: PrusaSlicer
tools.role: The slicer this project was authored in.
tools.install_hint: Only needed if you want to open the project with its original settings intact.

recommend_when.reason: This is a PrusaSlicer project. Its settings are readable there, but they do not carry over to the U1 — you still slice for the U1 in Snapmaker Orca.

tools.name: OrcaSlicer (upstream)
tools.role: The upstream slicer Snapmaker Orca is built from. Useful for printers other than the U1.
tools.install_hint: Only needed if you also print on a non-Snapmaker machine.

recommend_when.reason: This project targets another printer. If you actually want to print it on that machine, upstream OrcaSlicer is the closer match.

maturity_note: stable = an established, widely used tool. preview = a young or self-described experimental community project; Studio always shows its caution text before suggesting it.
